segments.title: What is Photosynthesis?
segments.narration: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn sunlight into chemical energy. It combines carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose and oxygen. This reaction powers plant growth and fuels the food chain.
segments.on_screen: Photosynthesis = Sunlight + CO₂ + H₂O → Glucose + O₂

segments.title: Light‑Dependent Reactions
segments.narration: In the thylakoid membranes, sunlight excites chlorophyll electrons. This energy splits water molecules, releasing oxygen and creating ATP and NADPH, the energy carriers for the next stage.

segments.title: Calvin Cycle (Light‑Independent)
segments.narration: Using ATP and NADPH, the Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into a three‑carbon sugar called G3P. Two G3P molecules combine to form one glucose molecule.

segments.title: Chlorophyll’s Role
segments.narration: Chlorophyll pigments absorb blue and red light, funneling the energy to reaction centers. This pigment gives leaves their green color and is essential for capturing solar energy.
segments.on_screen: Chlorophyll absorbs blue/red light → energy transfer

segments.title: Example: Leaf Cell
segments.narration: Inside a leaf cell, chloroplasts house the thylakoids and stroma where these reactions occur. The produced glucose fuels the plant, while oxygen exits through stomata.
segments.on_screen: Leaf cell → chloroplasts → glucose + O₂ release

segments.title: Example: Algae in Water
segments.narration: Algae perform photosynthesis in aquatic environments, providing oxygen for fish and forming the base of many food webs. Their rapid growth illustrates the efficiency of the process.
segments.on_screen: Algae → oxygen for water life + food source

segments.title: Why It Matters
segments.narration: Photosynthesis supplies the oxygen we breathe and the food we eat. Understanding it helps us appreciate ecosystems and develop sustainable energy solutions.
segments.on_screen: Photosynthesis = life support + renewable energy potential
